title: Underwriting Bulletin: Survey Age and the Elevation Row on HomeFlood Certificate Reviews
content:
**Scope.** This bulletin sets the elevation factor of the re-rated term premium when an Elevation Certificate review is completed on a HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies policy.

**Rule.**
- **Zones X, B, C and D.** For a property in zone X, B, C or D, the elevation factor is the tier's factor for a property outside a Special Flood Hazard Area, 1.0, whatever certificate is on file.
- **Any other zone.** The elevation factor follows the age of the certificate under review. Age is counted in whole calendar months from the certificate's survey date to the date Tidemark received it.
  - A certificate that shows a base flood elevation and was surveyed **fewer than 60** whole months before receipt takes the elevation table row for its elevation difference as certified.
  - A certificate that shows a base flood elevation and was surveyed **at least 60 but fewer than 120** whole months before receipt (120 being the 10-year maximum certificate age times 12) takes the elevation table row for its elevation difference **less one foot**, because Tidemark rates an older survey one foot more conservatively.
  - **Any other case** takes the tier's factor for a Special Flood Hazard Area property without an accepted certificate, 1.25. This covers a certificate showing no base flood elevation, a certificate surveyed 120 or more whole months before receipt, and a policy with no certificate.
- **Table ends.** A difference of 4 feet or more takes the "+4 or more" row, and one of -2 feet or lower takes the "-2 or lower" row.
- **Acceptance.** For a certificate review, and only for it, a certificate entry is accepted for rating when its survey date falls fewer than 120 whole calendar months (10 years times 12) before the date Tidemark received it. Tidemark records an Elevation Certificate entry only for a certificate on FEMA Form 086-0-33, completed and sealed by a licensed land surveyor, engineer or architect, for a building not altered since the survey.

A count of whole calendar months runs from the earlier date to the later one; the last month is not counted when the later date's day of the month falls before the earlier date's day of the month.

**The certificate under review** is the most recently received Elevation Certificate entry on the policy, read for its survey date, receipt date, base flood elevation and certified elevation difference. Where several entries share the latest receipt date, the one recorded first counts.

| Difference used (feet) | +4 or more | +3 | +2 | +1 | 0 | -1 | -2 or lower |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Elevation factor | 0.35 | 0.45 | 0.58 | 0.75 | 1.0 | 1.4 | 1.95 |

## Age bands at a glance (zone other than X, B, C or D; base flood elevation shown)

| Whole months from survey to receipt | Row used |
|---|---|
| 59 | difference as certified |
| 60 | difference less one foot |
| 119 | difference less one foot |
| 120 | no row; factor of 1.25 |

## Hypothetical cases

- Zone AE, certified difference +3 feet, survey 30 months before receipt: row +3, factor of 0.45.
- Zone AE, certified difference +3 feet, survey 84 months before receipt: row +2, factor of 0.58.
- Zone A, certified difference -1 foot, survey 72 months before receipt: -2 feet used, so the "-2 or lower" row applies, factor of 1.95.
- Zone AE, certificate without a base flood elevation: factor of 1.25.
- Zone X, any certificate: factor of 1.0.
- Survey on 20 March, received on 19 March five years later: 59 whole months, because the 19th falls before the 20th.
